answers.stem_only: Move the password into AWS Secrets Manager with managed automatic rotation for RDS (30-day schedule) and have the application fetch the secret at run time (ideally through the caching client) instead of reading a local file. Parameter Store has no native rotation; values pushed at launch go stale.

Use a Parameter Store parameter policy of type NoChangeNotification (90 days). Parameter policies need the advanced tier, so change the parameter to advanced, then catch the policy event with an Amazon EventBridge rule that notifies the team (for example through SNS).

ACM does not renew imported certificates. Obtain the renewed certificate from the same third-party CA and reimport it into ACM to the existing certificate ARN, so the listener keeps the same ARN and picks up the new certificate without reconfiguration.

Cross-account access to a secret needs two things: the secret must be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key whose key policy lets the account B role decrypt (the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager cannot be used cross-account because its key policy cannot be edited), and the secret needs a resource-based policy that grants GetSecretValue to that specific role (least privilege, not the whole account).

Terminate TLS on the Application Load Balancer with a public ACM certificate validated by DNS (CNAME in Route 53) so ACM renews and deploys it automatically; nothing is installed on the short-lived instances.

Create an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for Secrets Manager in the VPC with private DNS, and let the endpoint's security group accept HTTPS (443) from the rotation function's security group. Secrets Manager has no gateway endpoint; a NAT gateway is not private connectivity.

A secret deleted with default settings is only scheduled for deletion with a recovery window (30 days by default); cancel the deletion (restore the secret) so the same ARN works again with no application or policy changes.

Use Secrets Manager multi-Region secrets: replicate the primary secret to us-west-2 so rotation in us-east-1 propagates to the replica; in a Regional failure, promote the replica to a standalone secret.

Automatic rotation is required, which Parameter Store does not provide natively, so use Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; for lowest cost keep the default AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager rather than paying for a customer managed KMS key.

CloudFront only uses ACM certificates from US East (N. Virginia), and ACM certificates cannot be copied between Regions. Request a new public ACM certificate for app.example.com in us-east-1 and attach it to the distribution (alternate domain name app.example.com); keep the eu-west-1 certificate on the load balancer for origin HTTPS.

Use DNS validation and add the ACM-provided CNAME record to the Route 53 hosted zone (ACM can create it). While the record stays in place, ACM renews automatically with no human action; email validation needs someone to approve.

In the workload account, request a private certificate through ACM from the shared AWS Private CA and attach it to the HTTPS listener of the internal ALB; ACM manages renewal of private certificates it issued, and clients already trust the CA.

The value is non-sensitive configuration with no rotation need, so store it as a standard-tier String parameter in Parameter Store (no charge for standard parameters at standard throughput) and update it by hand.
